trust_decision.summary: The Shop API's mandatory public-only guard filters (Product.enabled = true, Collection.isPrivate = false, Facet.isPrivate = false) are merged into the caller's own filter object on each shop list query; because ListQueryBuilder applies the caller's filterOperator to every top-level filter key, an OR operator turns the guard into a disjunction and non-public rows are returned (CWE-200).

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names Shop API list queries and non-public entities; the first thing an engineer reads is the `products` query, which spreads caller `filter` and then adds `enabled: { eq: true }` while keeping the caller's `filterOperator`.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The lower-level service already re-derives the public guard itself with a hard AND (`options.filter.enabled.eq === true` -> `product.enabled = true`) for collection product lists, so that path looks protected; and the advisory names only Product.enabled / Collection.isPrivate / Facet.isPrivate, so a child-list guard on ProductVariant.enabled reads like a different concern.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The caller's own `filterOperator: OR` (and their own nested `_or` groups) must keep OR semantics across their own fields; only the guard may be AND-combined, so a fix that forces AND or drops the operator silently downgrades legitimate caller OR filters.

O6_input_shapes: filterOperator: LogicalOperator.OR with a flat caller filter
nested `_or: [...]` array inside the caller's filter object (default AND operator)
no filter / empty filter object (guard is the only condition)
caller filter with default AND operator

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Shop GraphQL Collection.productVariants(options: ProductVariantListOptions): the resolver merges `enabled: { eq: true }` into the caller filter but keeps the caller's filterOperator, so with `filterOperator: OR` a disabled ProductVariant of an enabled product is returned (the list query returns non-public entities), and this resolver was not changed by the published fix.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is a child list field rather than a top-level Shop API list query, and the service already applies `product.enabled = true` with a hard AND (product-variant.service.ts:229-231), so the collection is 'already guarded'.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package @vendure/core, different directory: api/resolvers/shop -> api/resolvers/entity, 1 file away

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Move the hand-written `result.enabled === false` public check of the single `product(id|slug)` query into a shared mandatory filter merged into a list query.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The same public-only rule is already written twice by hand (post-hoc check here, filter merge in `products`), so a maintainer consolidating the rule would plausibly route it through a filter/defaults merge too.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A shop-only `collection.products(options)`/`productVariants` defaults route that merges `isPrivate`/`enabled` guards the way `Query.collections` does.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Collection already exposes `productVariants` with exactly this merge, and the collection tree fields (`parent`, `children`) enforce privacy by hand at api/resolvers/entity/collection-entity.resolver.ts:114 and :129.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A filterOperator-aware guard inside the shop search/facetValue/collection count paths instead of the current post-hoc `.filter(!isPrivate)` pass.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The search plugin is a second implementation of the same public-only catalogue rule in a separate package directory, and its post-hoc filtering is the obvious thing a maintainer would later push into the query.

O9_family: information exposure / public-only catalog filter bypass (CWE-200, broken access control)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Force `filterOperator: LogicalOperator.AND` on the merged options (or spread the guard after clearing the operator), which fixes the guard but silently converts the caller's own OR filter into AND.
